regimes.note: Regimes group places with similar combined trends. They describe; they do not prove.

findings: 315 trend tests run. The usual test reports 279 pixels at p < 0.05; after removing month-to-month stickiness, 246 remain at p < 0.05, and 256 pass false-discovery control (10% across every test in this box). Separately, 4 cluster(s) are larger than the largest cluster on 95% of time-shuffled maps of all variables.
Wind speed at 2 m: calmer across 62 pixels around 30.5N, 75.6E (-0.0387 m/s per decade, cluster shuffle test p = 0.005).
Relative humidity: more humid across 63 pixels around 30.5N, 75.6E (+2.94 % per decade, cluster shuffle test p = 0.005).
Rainfall: wetter across 51 pixels around 30.7N, 75.8E (+0.16 mm/day per decade, cluster shuffle test p = 0.005).
Root-zone soil wetness: wetter soil across 49 pixels around 30.5N, 76.0E (+0.0182 0-1 per decade, cluster shuffle test p = 0.015).
Compound pattern: More humid and calmer in the same place (62 pixels) near 30.5N, 75.6E.
Compound pattern: Wetter and more humid in the same place (51 pixels) near 30.7N, 75.8E.
Compound pattern: Wetter and calmer in the same place (51 pixels) near 30.7N, 75.8E.
Trend regimes found by clustering: calmer + more humid + wetter (50 pixels); wetter + more humid + calmer (13 pixels).
caveats: NASA POWER here is MERRA-2-based reanalysis at about 0.5 degrees: a model constrained by observations, not a direct measurement.
Reanalysis can contain sudden jumps when the satellites feeding it change; a trend can partly be such a jump, especially for wind.
Linear trends only. Clusters show where change is stronger than chance, not why it happened.
